claims.assertion: Yazhi says advanced Lyrian-human civilizations on Earth repeatedly rise, flourish, and collapse in cycles of roughly 5,000–10,000 years.
claims.speaker: Yazhi
claims.qualifiers: She says Earth and human history are far older than conventional estimates and chronology is difficult because time is nonlinear.

claims.assertion: Yazhi says historical records can reflect multiple timelines rather than one linear past, complicating agreement about chronology.
claims.speaker: Yazhi
claims.qualifiers: She contrasts this with a simple arrow-like model of time.
